2026-11-09 semantics (manager's decision after the kernel engineer's design report): job_kill kills the whole subtree; a job that contains the caller is refused ERR_INVALID (so killing the root job is ERR_INVALID); process_spawn_in or job_create into a killed job answers ERR_PEER_CLOSED; a second job_kill is a no-op; nesting deeper than 8 answers ERR_NO_RESOURCES

2026-11-09 design J1 (chosen by the manager): upward parent pointers only (a job names its parent, keeps no child list); membership is read under the SCHED lock; job_kill marks the members through the existing process_kill path inside the SCHED lock, so no spawn can race the kill into a dying job

from WP-121's red team (2026-11-15, by reading, the manager read the same lines; nothing run, to check at activation): alloc_cluster scans the first FAT from its start for every allocation and FSInfo's next-free hint is never read (kernel/src/fs/fat32.rs:411); since WP-121 a write that extends a file asks first, one scan more than before (k+1 scans for k clusters), and walks the file's chain a second time, a FAT sector read for each cluster with no cache (kernel/src/fs/fat32.rs:389, kernel/src/fs/fat32.rs:764-768): an append to a 64 MiB file of 512-byte clusters walked 131072 links and now walks 262144, with the volume's lock held; a directory grows by a cluster for every 16 x sectors_per_cluster names (16 on the lab volume) and never shrinks (unlink marks the slot free and frees no directory cluster: kernel/src/fs/fat32.rs:676-702, kernel/src/fs/fat32.rs:862), and a lookup of a name that is not there reads the whole directory with the volume's lock held, an IrqSpinLock (kernel/src/fs/fat32.rs:536, kernel/src/fs/mod.rs:11): RSK-035; clusters of more than one sector are in no case (the lab volume has one sector to a cluster), so a count taken in sectors instead of clusters would pass every case

2026-11-15 design (services engineer; display.md v1.14): three options for the title in the compositor's own lines. (A) name it as ui.md §3.9 names a described value: `"`, C0/DEL/C1, U+2028/2029 and the bidi controls written [U+XXXX], plus every byte that does not begin a valid UTF-8 character as [U+FFFD] (the title is bytes, and a lone lead byte makes the narrator, user/apps/narrator/src/main.rs:55-65, swallow the closing quote); plain titles read as before; reversible by a version. (B) refuse CREATE_WINDOW/TITLE with such bytes: changes what every client may do under the frozen verbs (display.md v1.1/v1.3), and a quote is a fair character in a title; no existing client or expect file uses one (titles in the expect files: Sign in, Spy, Locked), but refusal moves the risk to every future client's error path. (C) strip them: silent loss, and a stripped title can become another's (`Sign in"` reads `Sign in`), an impersonation the escape avoids. Chosen: (A), re-implemented in displayd, not shared: displayd depends on libnawah and nawah-text only (user/apps/displayd/Cargo.toml), libui's put_quoted is private and writes libui's own 256-byte Text from decoded code points (user/libui/src/lib.rs:339, list.rs:119-127 pub(crate)); sharing would mean a public libui API or a move into nawah-text, both outside this package; both implementations are pinned by the same vectors (the quote, a newline, U+2028, U+202E, a long cut). Cut: the title gets 96 bytes in the line after naming; what does not fit is cut before the first unit (character or name) that does not fit, the line keeps its closing quote and event word and ends ` cut=<k>` (k units left out, at most 32); the mark goes at the end of the line, not right after the quote as in ui.md §3.9, so `" focused` and `" resized` stay adjacent for every reader; the line is at most 160 bytes, which the narrator's 256 holds even with every non-ASCII title byte written \u{…}. Storage: a title longer than TITLE_MAX is kept cut at a character boundary (drawing unchanged: draw_title already dropped the partial character, displayd main.rs:183-185). Failure modes: a title with the literal text [U+0022] or \u{0022} reads as a name (recorded limit, as ui.md §3.8/§3.9); invisible and quote-like characters pass as they are. Test: a new guest case TST-M5-WINDOW-TITLE (SVC-NT.TXT: the compositor and the narrator alone; no monitor step) with an exact transcript; SECURITY mutant M199 (the naming removed). The A11Y relay's attribution stays WP-103's.

found by the security red team and by the auditor while reading WP-118 on 2026-11-15 (by reading; nothing run, no CI evidence; the manager read the same lines): any process can lose the volume's free space for good, with no device fault: a file with no first cluster (new, empty or truncated) is written, in one call, more than the free space holds (a call takes up to 128 clusters); the call takes what is free, answers no space and loses it; the process then deletes files of its own and does it again, up to 127 clusters a round; the loss outlives a reboot and only a repair tool outside the system gives it back. A call on a file that has a first cluster loses nothing on a full disk: its new clusters stay linked to its chain past the size

design to decide in the package (2-3 options with trade-offs): store what was written and answer the shorter count when the disk fills in the middle of a call (the bytes are on the disk and the count says so; the next call answers no space with nothing taken; callers must treat a short count as they treat it elsewhere) against freeing what the call took and answering no space with the file as it was (all or nothing; more writes on the failure path, each of which can fail) against asking for the free count before taking anything (a scan of the FAT for every call)

Design chosen from the three options: when the volume runs out in the middle of a call, write stores what it wrote (the entry with the size reached) and answers that shorter count; when nothing could be written it answers no space with nothing taken; a count smaller than asked is already part of the ABI (a call is cut to 64 KiB) and by reading no caller breaks: config compares with the exact length and treats less as a failed save. Not chosen: freeing what the call took (all or nothing, but more writes on the failure path, each of which can fail, and bytes already written inside the old size would stay while the call says nothing was written) and asking for the free count first (a scan of the whole FAT for every call). 2026-11-15 design changed before the push (nothing of the first design was pushed): the auditor found that the design chosen at activation, a shorter count when the volume fills in the middle of a call, contradicts what the records already ask: PLAN-REVERSE section 4 item 8 recommends all or nothing for every call, and the planned oracle of TST-M6-DISK-FULL (WP-52) wants ERR_NO_SPACE with no partly written file; changing an acceptance text is the owner's, so the package took the design that needs no change to it: before any write the call counts the clusters it needs beyond the file's chain and asks the allocator whether it can take them (a scan of the first FAT that stops at the last one needed; the volume's lock is held to the end of the call); when it cannot, the call answers no space with nothing written and nothing taken. No write is added: the writes of TST-M3-FAT32-FAULT-WRITE keep their order and counts. The test kernel's hook no longer answers for the allocator: it ends the allocator's range before a chosen free cluster and the allocator's own scan answers.
